newsitem.title: USA: CBOT Nov soybeans end up as deliveries stopped.
newsitem.headline: CBOT Nov soybeans end up as deliveries stopped.

text.p: CBOT November soybean futures closed higher on another day of strong stopping of deliveries posted against that month, traders said.
"There was no farmer selling and ADM stopped the beans," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

The ADM Investor Services house account stopped 740,000 bushels of the 745,000 posted Friday for delivery on the November contract. Friday was the third consecutive session ADM surfaced as a strong commercial stopper of the soybean deliveries.
Traders said short covering boosted the market.

Position squaring was noted before the release late Friday of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders Report. Also the market was evening-up for the weekend amid positioning before the release Tuesday of USDA's November crop production report.
The Leslie-ADM Elevator survey released early Friday showed 1996 U.S. soybean production at 2.38 billion bushels, above an average analysts' estimate of 2.376 billion.
Soybeans closed 1-1/4 cents per bushel higher to 3-1/4 lower, with November up 1-1/4 at $6.87-3/4.
Traders said the soybean market found significant underpinning from the gains in corn and wheat.
"Commercial buying in wheat and corn kept the market up all day," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
He also said, "There's a lot of talk ADM may make the play (delivery) good," referring to trade speculation that ADM may not redeliver the beans it stopped this week.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 48,000 contracts, below the 51,470 traded Thursday, according to the CBOT.
In soybean options, Cargill Investor Services bought 400 July $7.00 puts, sold 400 July $6.25 calls and sold 400 July $7.50 calls, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, up from 14,642 Thursday.
